questions.explain: Multiply and divide the coefficients: 1.2 × 3.0 = 3.6, and 3.6 ÷ 9.0 = 0.4. Combine the powers: −3 + 8 − (−2) = 7, so the result is 0.4 × 10⁷ = 4.0 × 10⁶. 4.0 × 10⁷ rewrites 0.4 as 4 without lowering the exponent, 4.0 × 10⁸ moves the exponent the wrong way, 4.0 × 10² subtracts 2 instead of adding it for the ÷ 10⁻², and 2.5 × 10⁶ divides the coefficients the wrong way round (9 ÷ 3.6).

questions.stem: A coolant pump motor draws 2.4 MW steadily for 15 minutes. How much energy does it use, in kilojoules?
questions.explain: Energy = power × time = (2.4 × 10⁶ W)(900 s) = 2.16 × 10⁹ J, and dividing by 1,000 gives 2.16 × 10⁶ kJ. 2.16 × 10⁹ kJ leaves the answer in joules, 2.16 × 10³ kJ reads mega as 10³, 3.6 × 10⁴ kJ uses 15 seconds instead of 900, and 6.0 × 10⁵ kJ multiplies by 0.25 hour, which gives watt-hours, not joules.

questions.stem: For positive x and y, (27x⁶y⁻³)^(2/3) ÷ (3x²y)⁻¹ simplifies to
questions.explain: 27^(2/3) = (∛27)² = 9, x^(6 × 2/3) = x⁴ and y^(−3 × 2/3) = y⁻², so the first part is 9x⁴y⁻². Dividing by (3x²y)⁻¹ is the same as multiplying by 3x²y, giving 27x⁶y⁻¹ = 27x⁶/y. 3x²/y³ divides by 3x²y, ignoring the −1 power, 54x⁶/y reads 27^(2/3) as 27 × 2/3 = 18, 27x⁸/y multiplies the x exponents 4 × 2 instead of adding, and 9x⁶/y drops the 3.

questions.stem: (√12 + √27)² is equal to
questions.explain: Simplify first: √12 = 2√3 and √27 = 3√3, so the sum is 5√3, and (5√3)² = 25 × 3 = 75. Expanding gives the same: 12 + 2√324 + 27 = 12 + 36 + 27 = 75. 39 squares each term and drops the middle term, 57 includes the middle term once instead of twice, 225 squares 5 × 3 = 15, and 5√3 stops before squaring.

questions.stem: 6/(3 − √3) is equal to
questions.explain: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate 3 + √3: the bottom becomes 9 − 3 = 6, and 6(3 + √3)/6 = 3 + √3. 3 − √3 keeps the original sign, (3 + √3)/2 adds 9 + 3 = 12 in the denominator, 6 + 2√3 divides by 3 instead of 6, and 18 + 6√3 forgets the denominator altogether.

Write both sides as powers of 2: 2^(3x + 3) = 2^(5x − 5). Equal bases mean equal exponents, so 3x + 3 = 5x − 5, 8 = 2x and x = 4. −4 is a sign slip when collecting terms, 7 writes 32 as 2⁴, 1 forgets to distribute (3x + 1 = 5x − 1), and 8 stops at 2x = 8.

questions.stem: A detector circuit carries a steady current of 450 μA for 2.0 hours. How much charge passes through it?
questions.explain: Q = It = (450 × 10⁻⁶ A)(7,200 s) = 3.24 C. 0.054 C uses 120 s (minutes, not seconds), 0.90 C uses 2,000 s, 3,240 C reads micro as milli, and 3.24 × 10⁻³ C reads micro as nano.

(−2)⁻³ = 1/(−8) = −1/8, 2⁻² = 1/4, and (1/4)^(−1/2) = 4^(1/2) = 2. So −1/8 − 2/8 + 16/8 = 13/8. 15/8 makes (−2)⁻³ positive, 1/8 takes (1/4)^(−1/2) as 1/2 instead of flipping it, 17/8 adds the 1/4 instead of subtracting it, and −19/8 reads the negative exponent as a negative sign, making the last term −2.

questions.stem: A cube has a volume of 2.7 × 10⁻⁵ m³. What is the length of one edge?
questions.explain: Rewrite so the power of ten divides by 3: 2.7 × 10⁻⁵ = 27 × 10⁻⁶ m³, and ∛(27 × 10⁻⁶) = 3 × 10⁻² m = 3.0 cm. 0.30 cm and 30 cm are slips of one and three places in the m to cm step, 1.4 cm takes the cube root of 2.7 as if the number were 2.7 × 10⁻⁶, and 0.52 cm takes a square root instead of a cube root.

questions.stem: Two resistors in parallel satisfy 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂. Solved for R₂, this is
questions.explain: Isolate the term: 1/R₂ = 1/R − 1/R₁ = (R₁ − R)/(RR₁). Flip both sides: R₂ = RR₁/(R₁ − R). Check with R₁ = 6 Ω and R₂ = 3 Ω, which give R = 2 Ω: 2 × 6/(6 − 2) = 3 ✓. RR₁/(R − R₁) reverses the subtraction and gives a negative resistance, R − R₁ treats reciprocals as if they subtract directly, RR₁/(R + R₁) uses the wrong sign, and (R₁ − R)/(RR₁) is 1/R₂, not R₂.

questions.stem: The period of a pendulum is T = 2π√(L/g). Solved for g, this is
questions.explain: Divide by 2π: T/(2π) = √(L/g). Square: T²/(4π²) = L/g. Cross-multiply: g = 4π²L/T². 2πL/T² forgets to square the 2π, 4π²T²/L turns the fraction upside down, 4π²L/T forgets to square T, and L/(4π²T²) multiplies by T² instead of dividing by it.

questions.stem: A technician mixes a 30% solution with an 80% solution to make 50 L of a 62% solution. How many liters of the 80% solution are used?
questions.explain: Let x be liters of 80%: 0.80x + 0.30(50 − x) = 0.62 × 50 = 31. So 0.50x + 15 = 31 and x = 32 L. 18 L is the amount of 30% solution, 25 L assumes equal parts, 31 L is the liters of pure solute, and 20 L uses 50 × (62 − 30)/80, dividing by the wrong spread (it should be 80 − 30 = 50).

questions.stem: Solve the system 2x + 3y = 7 and 5x − 2y = 27. The solution (x, y) is
questions.explain: Multiply the first equation by 2 and the second by 3: 4x + 6y = 14 and 15x − 6y = 81. Adding gives 19x = 95, so x = 5, and 10 + 3y = 7 gives y = −1. Check: 25 + 2 = 27 ✓. (5, 1) drops the sign of 3y = −3, (−1, 5) swaps x and y, (4, −1/3) fits only the first equation, and (6, 3/2) fits only the second.

Distribute: −6x + 15 ≥ 4x + 35, so −10x ≥ 20. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality: x ≤ −2. x ≥ −2 forgets to reverse, x ≤ −5 distributes −3 × −5 as −15, x ≤ 2 drops the sign of the 20, and x ≥ −5 makes both of the last two slips at once.

questions.stem: How many integers x satisfy |2x − 7| < 9?
questions.explain: |2x − 7| < 9 means −9 < 2x − 7 < 9. Add 7: −2 < 2x < 16, so −1 < x < 8. The integers are 0 through 7, which is 8 of them. 6 slips the sign of −9 + 7 and starts at x > 1, 7 counts only the positive integers 1 to 7, 9 includes the endpoint 8, and 10 includes both endpoints as if the sign were ≤.

questions.stem: Solve |x − 6| = 2x + 3.
questions.explain: Case 1: x − 6 = 2x + 3 gives x = −9, but then the right side is −15, and an absolute value can't equal a negative number, so it is rejected. Case 2: x − 6 = −(2x + 3) gives 3x = 3, x = 1, and |1 − 6| = 5 = 2(1) + 3 ✓. Keeping both skips the check, x = −9 only keeps the wrong one, x = 3 negates only the 2x in case 2, and No solution rejects the valid root as well.

questions.stem: Pump A fills a tank in 6 hours and pump B fills it in 4 hours. A drain empties the full tank in 12 hours. With both pumps running and the drain open, how long does it take to fill the empty tank?
questions.explain: Add the rates, with the drain negative: 1/6 + 1/4 − 1/12 = 2/12 + 3/12 − 1/12 = 4/12 = 1/3 tank per hour, so the tank fills in 3 hours. 2.4 h ignores the drain, 2 h adds the drain as if it helped, 7 1/3 h averages the three times, and 1/3 h reports the rate instead of the time.

questions.stem: The Fahrenheit and kelvin scales are related by F = 1.8(K − 273.15) + 32. At what temperature, to the nearest tenth, do the two scales read the same number?
questions.explain: Set F = K: K = 1.8K − 491.67 + 32 = 1.8K − 459.67, so 0.8K = 459.67 and K = 574.5875, which rounds to 574.6. −40.0 is where Celsius and Fahrenheit agree, 459.7 drops the 0.8 and stops at 459.67, 654.6 subtracts the 32 instead of adding it, and −269.4 uses 5/9 in place of 1.8.

questions.stem: Which line passes through (−2, 5) and is perpendicular to 3x − 4y = 12?
questions.explain: 3x − 4y = 12 is y = (3/4)x − 3, slope 3/4. A perpendicular line has the negative reciprocal slope, −4/3. Through (−2, 5): y − 5 = −(4/3)(x + 2), so y = −(4/3)x − 8/3 + 5 = −(4/3)x + 7/3. (3/4)x + 13/2 is the parallel line, (4/3)x + 23/3 flips the slope but forgets the sign, −(3/4)x + 7/2 changes the sign but forgets to flip, and −(4/3)x + 23/3 adds 8/3 instead of subtracting it.

questions.stem: For which values of k does kx² + 6x + 3 = 0 have two distinct real roots?
questions.explain: Two distinct real roots need b² − 4ac > 0: 36 − 12k > 0, so k < 3. Also k can't be 0, or the equation is no longer quadratic and has only one root. k < 3 forgets that k ≠ 0, k > 3 reverses the inequality, k ≤ 3 lets the discriminant be 0 (one repeated root), and k < 1/2 uses b = 6 instead of b² = 36.

questions.stem: Solve 2x² − 4x − 5 = 0.
questions.explain: x = [4 ± √(16 − 4(2)(−5))]/4 = (4 ± √56)/4. √56 = 2√14, so x = (4 ± 2√14)/4 = (2 ± √14)/2. (−2 ± √14)/2 uses +b instead of −b, 2 ± √14 divides by a instead of 2a, (4 ± √14)/4 drops the 2 when simplifying √56, and 5/2 or −1/2 uses 2ac instead of 4ac, giving √36 = 6.

questions.stem: A test projectile's height is h(t) = −4.9t² + 29.4t + 12, with h in meters and t in seconds. What is its maximum height?
questions.explain: The vertex is at t = −b/(2a) = −29.4/(−9.8) = 3 s, and h(3) = −44.1 + 88.2 + 12 = 56.1 m. 44.1 m forgets the starting height of 12, 144.3 m adds the −4.9t² term instead of subtracting it, 12.0 m uses t = −b/a = 6 s, which is when the projectile is back at 12 m, and 100.2 m drops the t² term.

questions.stem: Solve 6x² − x − 15 = 0.
questions.explain: 6x² − x − 15 = (2x + 3)(3x − 5), since −10x + 9x = −x. Set each factor to zero: x = −3/2 or x = 5/3. 3/2 and −5/3 flip both signs, −3 and 5 drop the coefficients of x, −2/3 and 3/5 turn each root upside down, and 1/6 and −5/2 are the sum and product of the roots, not the roots.

questions.stem: A rectangular shield plate has an area of 120 cm² and a perimeter of 46 cm. What is the length of its diagonal?
questions.explain: l + w = 23 and lw = 120, so the sides are the roots of t² − 23t + 120 = 0, which factors as (t − 15)(t − 8). The diagonal is √(15² + 8²) = √289 = 17 cm. 23 cm is l + w, 15.6 cm uses 12 × 10 (right area, wrong perimeter), 20.9 cm uses 20 × 6, and 11.0 cm is √120, the side of a square with that area.

questions.stem: What is the vertex of y = 2x² − 12x + 7?
questions.explain: y = 2(x² − 6x) + 7 = 2[(x − 3)² − 9] + 7 = 2(x − 3)² − 11, so the vertex is (3, −11). (−3, 61) takes the wrong sign of the x-coordinate, (3, −2) subtracts 9 without multiplying by the 2 outside, (3, 25) adds the 18 instead of subtracting it, and (6, 7) uses −b/a instead of −b/(2a).

questions.stem: One root of x² + bx + 18 = 0 is twice the other. What are the possible values of b?
questions.explain: Call the roots r and 2r. Their product is 2r² = 18, so r = 3 or r = −3. Their sum is 3r = −b, so b = −9 or b = 9. 9 only forgets the second case, 3 or −3 reports r instead of b, 9√2 or −9√2 uses r² = 18 instead of 2r² = 18, and 6 or −6 takes the sum as 2r.

questions.stem: Solve x² − 2x − 15 ≤ 0.
questions.explain: x² − 2x − 15 = (x − 5)(x + 3), with roots −3 and 5. An upward parabola is at or below zero between its roots, so −3 ≤ x ≤ 5. x ≤ −3 or x ≥ 5 gives where it is positive, −5 ≤ x ≤ 3 flips the signs of the roots, x ≤ 5 ignores the left root, and −3 < x < 5 drops the equality.

questions.stem: If f(x) = 2x − 3 and g(x) = x² + 1, what is f(g(−2)) − g(f(−2))?
questions.explain: g(−2) = 5, so f(g(−2)) = f(5) = 7. f(−2) = −7, so g(f(−2)) = g(−7) = 50. Then 7 − 50 = −43. 43 subtracts in the wrong order, 0 assumes the order of composition doesn't matter, −35 multiplies f(−2) × g(−2) instead of composing, and 57 adds the two values.

questions.stem: If f(x) = (3x − 2)/(x + 4), then f⁻¹(x) =
questions.explain: Write y = (3x − 2)/(x + 4) and solve for x: xy + 4y = 3x − 2, so x(y − 3) = −4y − 2 and x = (4y + 2)/(3 − y). Swap the letters: f⁻¹(x) = (4x + 2)/(3 − x). Check: f(3) = 7/7 = 1 and f⁻¹(1) = 6/2 = 3 ✓. (x + 4)/(3x − 2) is the reciprocal 1/f, not the inverse, (4x − 2)/(3 − x) drops a sign on the 2, (4x + 2)/(x − 3) drops the sign on the denominator, and (3x + 2)/(x − 4) just reverses each sign.

questions.stem: What is the domain of f(x) = √(x + 3)/(x² − 4)?
questions.explain: The square root needs x + 3 ≥ 0, so x ≥ −3, and the denominator can't be zero, so x ≠ 2 and x ≠ −2 (both lie in x ≥ −3). x > −3, x ≠ 2 wrongly excludes −3, where the root is 0, and misses −2. x ≥ −3, x ≠ 2 misses −2. x ≠ ±2 alone ignores the square root, and x ≥ 3 drops the sign of the 3.

questions.stem: If f(x) = 3x² − 2x, then f(a + 1) − f(a) =
questions.explain: f(a + 1) = 3(a² + 2a + 1) − 2a − 2 = 3a² + 4a + 1. Subtract f(a) = 3a² − 2a: 3a² + 4a + 1 − 3a² + 2a = 6a + 1. 6a + 3 forgets the −2 from −2(a + 1), 3a² + 4a + 1 is f(a + 1) alone, 1 expands (a + 1)² as a² + 1, and 6a − 1 slips a sign when subtracting f(a).

questions.stem: A linear function has f(2) = 11 and f(7) = −4. What is f(−1)?
questions.explain: Slope = (−4 − 11)/(7 − 2) = −15/5 = −3. Going from x = 2 to x = −1 is 3 steps left, so f(−1) = 11 + (−3)(−3) = 20. 2 uses a slope of +3, 12 uses the upside-down slope −1/3, 14 moves only one step, and −3 is the slope, not the value.

questions.stem: f(x) = 4x + k and g(x) = 2x − 5. For what value of k is f(g(x)) = g(f(x)) for all x?
questions.explain: f(g(x)) = 4(2x − 5) + k = 8x − 20 + k and g(f(x)) = 2(4x + k) − 5 = 8x + 2k − 5. Setting them equal: −20 + k = 2k − 5, so k = −15. Check: both constants are −35 ✓. 15 is a sign slip, −5 copies g's constant, −25 adds −20 and −5, and No value of k comes from forgetting to double k in g(f(x)), which leaves −20 + k = k − 5.

questions.stem: If f(x) = 2^(x − 1) + 3, what is f⁻¹(19)?
questions.explain: f⁻¹(19) is the x that makes f(x) = 19: 2^(x − 1) = 16 = 2⁴, so x − 1 = 4 and x = 5. Check: f(5) = 16 + 3 = 19 ✓. 4 forgets to add the 1 back, 8 halves 16 instead of taking the log, 262,147 computes f(19) instead of f⁻¹(19), and 1/19 treats the inverse as a reciprocal.

questions.stem: log₂ 48 − log₂ 3 + 2 log₂ √2 is equal to
questions.explain: log₂ 48 − log₂ 3 = log₂ 16 = 4, and 2 log₂ √2 = log₂ (√2)² = log₂ 2 = 1. Total: 5. 4 drops the last term, 4.5 uses log₂ √2 = 0.5 and forgets the 2, 6 treats 2 log₂ √2 as 2, and 16 stops at 48 ÷ 3 without taking the log.

questions.stem: Solve 5^(2x) = 3^(x + 1), to the nearest hundredth.
questions.explain: Take natural logs: 2x ln 5 = (x + 1) ln 3. Collect x: x(2 ln 5 − ln 3) = ln 3, so x = 1.0986/(3.2189 − 1.0986) = 1.0986/2.1203 ≈ 0.52. 2.15 drops the 2 in front of ln 5, 0.25 adds ln 3 instead of subtracting it, 0.47 expands (x + 1) ln 3 as x ln 3 + 1, and 0.34 forgets the x on the right side.

questions.stem: Iodine-131 has a half-life of 8.0 days. A source has an activity of 640 mCi. What is its activity 20 days later, to the nearest mCi?
questions.explain: 20 days is 20/8 = 2.5 half-lives, so A = 640 × (1/2)^2.5 = 640 × 0.17678 ≈ 113 mCi. 160 mCi rounds down to 2 half-lives, 80 mCi rounds up to 3, 128 mCi divides by 2 × 2.5 = 5, and 256 mCi divides by 2.5. Fractional half-lives need the exponent, not a rounded count.

questions.stem: Cobalt-60 has a half-life of 5.27 years. How long does a source take to decay to 10% of its original activity?
questions.explain: (1/2)^n = 0.10 gives n = log₂ 10 = 3.32 half-lives, and 3.32 × 5.27 ≈ 17.5 years. 47.4 years assumes 10% is lost each half-life (9 half-lives), 52.7 years uses 10 half-lives, 26.4 years uses 5, and 12.1 years multiplies by ln 10 instead of log₂ 10.

questions.stem: During a reactor startup, power rises as P = P₀e^(t/τ) with a stable period τ = 60 s. About how long does power take to rise from 1.0% to 100%?
questions.explain: 100%/1.0% = 100 = e^(t/60), so t = 60 ln 100 = 60 × 4.605 ≈ 276 s. 120 s uses the common log (log 100 = 2), 399 s uses log₂ 100 as if τ were a doubling time, 5,940 s treats the rise as linear (99 × 60), and 6,000 s multiplies 60 by 100.

questions.stem: A quantity grows by 7% per year, compounded yearly. To the nearest tenth of a year, how long does it take to double?
questions.explain: 1.07^t = 2, so t = ln 2/ln 1.07 = 0.6931/0.06766 ≈ 10.2 years. 14.3 years is 100/7, simple growth with no compounding, 10.0 years is the rule of 70, 9.9 years is the rule of 69.3 (both are estimates, not the nearest tenth), and 4.3 years divides log 2 by 0.07.

questions.stem: Solve log₃(x + 6) + log₃(x − 2) = 2.
questions.explain: Combine: log₃[(x + 6)(x − 2)] = 2, so (x + 6)(x − 2) = 9, x² + 4x − 21 = 0 and (x + 7)(x − 3) = 0. x = −7 makes both logs undefined, so only x = 3 works: log₃ 9 + log₃ 1 = 2 + 0 ✓. Keeping −7 skips the domain check, −7 only keeps the wrong root, 5/2 adds the insides instead of multiplying them, and −2 + 3√2 sets the product equal to 2 instead of 3² = 9.

questions.stem: Sound intensity level is β = 10 log(I/I₀) decibels. If the intensity of a noise source is multiplied by 250, by how much does its level rise, to the nearest tenth?
questions.explain: Δβ = 10 log 250 = 10 × 2.398 ≈ 24.0 dB. 2.4 dB forgets the factor of 10, 48.0 dB uses 20 log, which is for amplitudes, not intensity, 55.2 dB uses the natural log, and 2,500 dB multiplies 10 × 250 with no log at all.

questions.stem: A sample's count rate falls from 4,800 to 1,350 counts per minute in 6.0 hours. What is its half-life, to the nearest tenth of an hour?
questions.explain: The fraction left is 1,350/4,800 = 0.28125, so the number of half-lives is n = log₂(4,800/1,350) = log₂ 3.556 ≈ 1.83. Half-life = 6.0/1.83 ≈ 3.3 h. 3.0 h calls 0.28 a quarter (exactly 2 half-lives), 4.2 h treats the decay as linear, 1.8 h reports the number of half-lives as hours, and 11.0 h multiplies 6.0 × 1.83 instead of dividing.

questions.stem: Given log 2 = 0.301 and log 3 = 0.477, what is log 7.2?
questions.explain: 7.2 = 72/10 = 2³ × 3²/10, so log 7.2 = 3(0.301) + 2(0.477) − 1 = 0.903 + 0.954 − 1 = 0.857. 1.857 is log 72 (forgets the ÷ 10), 1.033 swaps the powers, 2(0.301) + 3(0.477) − 1, which is log 10.8, 2.857 adds 1 instead of subtracting it, and −0.143 is log 0.72 (divides by 100).

questions.stem: Coolant flow is raised 30%, then cut by 30%, then raised 10%. Compared with the original flow, the final flow is
questions.explain: Multiply the factors: 1.30 × 0.70 × 1.10 = 0.91 × 1.10 = 1.001, which is a 0.1% increase. A 10% increase adds the percents (30 − 30 + 10), a 9% decrease stops after the first two changes, no change assumes up 30 and down 30 cancel exactly, and a 1% increase misplaces the decimal in 1.001.

questions.stem: After a 15% reduction, a pressure reading is 1,904 psi. What was the reading before the reduction?
questions.explain: After the cut, 85% remains: 0.85P = 1,904, so P = 1,904 ÷ 0.85 = 2,240 psi. 2,189.6 psi adds 15% of the new value (15% of the wrong base), 1,618.4 psi takes 15% off again, 1,919 psi adds 15 psi, and 12,693 psi divides by 0.15, the part removed, instead of 0.85, the part left.

questions.stem: Radiation intensity from a point source varies inversely with the square of the distance. It is 360 mR/h at 2.0 m. At what distance is it 10 mR/h?
questions.explain: I × d² is constant: 360 × 2.0² = 10 × d², so d² = 144 and d = 12 m. Equivalently, the intensity falls by 36, so the distance grows by √36 = 6, and 2.0 × 6 = 12. 72 m uses inverse (not inverse square) variation, 6.0 m forgets to multiply by the starting 2.0 m, 36 m uses the ratio as the distance, and 6.6 m takes a cube root.

questions.stem: Power dissipated in a resistor is P = I²R. If the current rises 50% and the resistance falls 20%, the power
questions.explain: New power factor: (1.5)² × 0.8 = 2.25 × 0.8 = 1.8, so power rises 80%. 30% subtracts the percents, 20% forgets to square the current (1.5 × 0.8 = 1.2), 125% ignores the resistance change (2.25), and 180% reads the factor 1.8 as the increase.

questions.stem: y varies directly as x² and inversely as √z. If y = 12 when x = 2 and z = 9, what is y when x = 3 and z = 36?
questions.explain: y = kx²/√z, so 12 = k(4)/3 and k = 9. Then y = 9(9)/√36 = 81/6 = 13.5. 6.75 divides by z instead of √z, 9 uses x instead of x², 27 ignores z altogether, and 10.7 swaps which quantity is direct and which is inverse.

questions.stem: On a submarine the ratio of officers to enlisted crew is 2:13. After 6 more officers report aboard and 3 enlisted crew leave, the ratio is 1:5. How many people were aboard at first?
questions.explain: Let the crew be 2k officers and 13k enlisted. Then (2k + 6)/(13k − 3) = 1/5, so 10k + 30 = 13k − 3 and k = 11. That's 22 officers and 143 enlisted, 165 in all. Check: 28:140 = 1:5 ✓. 168 is the total after the changes, 171 adds the 6 arrivals but forgets the 3 who left, 22 is the officers only, and 143 is the enlisted only.

questions.stem: A tank holds 40 L of a 12% boric acid solution. How much water must evaporate to raise the concentration to 15%?
questions.explain: The acid stays at 0.12 × 40 = 4.8 L. At 15%, the total must be 4.8/0.15 = 32 L, so 40 − 32 = 8 L evaporates. 1.2 L takes 3% of 40, 10 L uses 25% of 40 because 15/12 = 1.25, 32 L is the final volume, and 4.8 L is the amount of acid.

questions.stem: A lab measures g as 9.62 m/s². The accepted value is 9.81 m/s². What is the percent error, to the nearest tenth?
questions.explain: Percent error = |9.62 − 9.81|/9.81 × 100 = 0.19/9.81 × 100 ≈ 1.9%. 2.0% divides by the measured value instead of the accepted one, 0.19% forgets to divide, 98.1% is the ratio 9.62/9.81 as a percent, and 19.4% misplaces the decimal.

questions.stem: A ship's fuel burn rate, in gallons per hour, varies as the cube of its speed. If speed goes from 12 knots to 15 knots, by about what percent does the fuel burned per nautical mile increase?
questions.explain: Fuel per mile = (fuel per hour) ÷ (miles per hour), which varies as v³/v = v². The factor is (15/12)² = 1.25² = 1.5625, about a 56% increase. 95% is the rise in fuel per hour (1.25³ = 1.953), 25% is the speed increase, 75% multiplies 25% by 3, and 144% uses the fourth power.

questions.stem: Three identical pumps move 4,500 gallons in 50 minutes. How long do five of these pumps take to move 9,000 gallons?
questions.explain: Each pump moves 4,500/(3 × 50) = 30 gal/min, so five move 150 gal/min, and 9,000/150 = 60 minutes. 100 min doubles the time for the doubled volume but ignores the extra pumps, 166.7 min treats more pumps as more time, 83.3 min also scales the wrong way and forgets the doubled volume, and 30 min scales for the pumps but forgets the volume doubled.

questions.stem: A bin holds 5 good valves and 3 defective valves. Two are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that at least one is defective?
questions.explain: Use the complement. P(both good) = 5/8 × 4/7 = 20/56 = 5/14, so P(at least one defective) = 1 − 5/14 = 9/14. 39/64 replaces the first valve (1 − 25/64), 3/28 is both defective, 15/28 is exactly one defective, and 5/14 is both good.

questions.stem: A 4-person inspection team is chosen from 6 officers and 5 enlisted. How many teams include at least 2 officers?
questions.explain: All teams: C(11, 4) = 330. Subtract teams with no officers, C(5, 4) = 5, and with exactly one, 6 × C(5, 3) = 60: 330 − 65 = 265. 540 picks 2 officers and then any 2 of the other 9, which counts many teams more than once, 150 counts exactly 2 officers only, 325 subtracts only the no-officer teams, and 270 subtracts only the one-officer teams.

questions.stem: A 4-letter access code uses the letters A to F with no letter repeated, and must start with a vowel (A or E). How many codes are possible?
questions.explain: 2 choices for the first letter, then 5, 4 and 3 for the rest: 2 × 5 × 4 × 3 = 120. 360 ignores the vowel rule (6 × 5 × 4 × 3), 432 allows repeats (2 × 6³), 250 allows repeats among the last three but not the first (2 × 5³), and 20 ignores order (2 × C(5, 3)).

questions.stem: Three independent alarms each detect a fault with probability 0.9. What is the probability that exactly two of them detect it?
questions.explain: Each way for exactly two to detect has probability 0.9 × 0.9 × 0.1 = 0.081, and there are 3 ways (which alarm misses), so 3 × 0.081 = 0.243. 0.081 forgets the 3 ways, 0.729 is all three detecting, 0.972 is at least two, and 0.270 uses 0.9 × 0.1 × 3, leaving out one 0.9.

questions.stem: A course grade is 50% tests, 20% quizzes and 30% final exam. A student averages 82 on tests and 90 on quizzes. What final exam score, to the nearest tenth, gives an 85 overall?
questions.explain: 0.50(82) + 0.20(90) + 0.30F = 85, so 41 + 18 + 0.30F = 85, 0.30F = 26 and F ≈ 86.7. 83.0 averages the three scores equally, 84.8 swaps the test and final weights, 26.0 stops before dividing by 0.30, and 85.0 assumes the final must match the target.

questions.stem: Nine readings have a mean of 42. When one reading is removed, the other eight have a mean of 40.5. What was the removed reading?
questions.explain: The nine readings total 9 × 42 = 378 and the eight total 8 × 40.5 = 324, so the removed reading is 378 − 324 = 54. 1.5 is the change in the mean, 13.5 is 9 × 1.5, 55.5 adds 9 × 1.5 to 42 instead of 8 × 1.5, and 43.5 adds only 1.5.

questions.stem: The data set 14, 9, 22, 17, 9, 31, 12, x has a median of 15. What is x?
questions.explain: Sorted without x: 9, 9, 12, 14, 17, 22, 31. With 8 values the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th. For a median of 15, x must sit between 14 and 17, so (14 + x)/2 = 15 and x = 16. 15 sets x equal to the median, which gives (14 + 15)/2 = 14.5, 6 makes the mean 15 instead of the median, and 17 or 18 leave 14 and 17 in the middle, a median of 15.5.

questions.stem: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is at least 10?
questions.explain: Favorable ordered outcomes: (4, 6), (6, 4), (5, 5), (5, 6), (6, 5), (6, 6), which is 6 of 36 = 1/6. 1/12 counts unordered pairs (3 of 36), 5/36 forgets (6, 6), 5/18 includes sums of 9, and 3/11 treats the 11 possible sums as equally likely.

questions.stem: In a class, 60% of students pass math, 50% pass physics and 40% pass both. If a student passed physics, what is the probability the student passed math?
questions.explain: P(math | physics) = P(both)/P(physics) = 0.40/0.50 = 0.80. 0.67 divides by P(math) instead, 0.30 multiplies 0.60 × 0.50 as if they were independent, 0.40 is P(both) with no condition, and 0.70 is P(math or physics).

questions.stem: Independent events A and B have P(A) = 0.30 and P(B) = 0.45. What is the probability that exactly one of them occurs?
questions.explain: P(A and not B) + P(B and not A) = 0.30 × 0.55 + 0.70 × 0.45 = 0.165 + 0.315 = 0.48. 0.75 adds the probabilities, 0.615 is P(A or B), which includes both, 0.135 is P(both), and 0.385 is P(neither).

Work out the denominator first: 1.6 × 2.0 = 3.2 and 10³ × 10⁻⁵ = 10⁻², so it is 3.2 × 10⁻². Then 4.8 ÷ 3.2 = 1.5 and 10⁻⁷ ÷ 10⁻² = 10⁻⁵, giving 1.5 × 10⁻⁵. 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁵ subtracts both denominator exponents as if they were +3 and +5, 1.5 × 10⁻⁹ subtracts +2 instead of −2, 3.0 × 10⁻⁵ leaves the 2.0 out of the denominator, and 1.5 × 10⁵ flips the sign of the final exponent.

questions.stem: A reactor plant produces 3.2 GW of thermal power steadily for 30 days. How much thermal energy is that, in joules?
questions.explain: Energy = power × time in seconds. 30 days = 30 × 24 × 3,600 = 2.592 × 10⁶ s, and 3.2 GW = 3.2 × 10⁹ W, so E = 3.2 × 10⁹ × 2.592 × 10⁶ ≈ 8.29 × 10¹⁵ J. 1.38 × 10¹⁴ J uses minutes instead of seconds, 2.30 × 10¹² J uses hours, 8.29 × 10¹² J reads giga as 10⁶, and 9.60 × 10¹⁰ J multiplies by 30 without converting days at all.

questions.stem: For x > 0, (8x⁻⁶)^(−2/3) · (4x³)^(1/2) simplifies to
questions.explain: (8x⁻⁶)^(−2/3) = 8^(−2/3) · x^((−6)(−2/3)) = (1/4)x⁴. (4x³)^(1/2) = 2x^(3/2). Multiply: (1/4)(2) x^(4 + 3/2) = x^(11/2)/2. 8x^(11/2) drops the minus sign on the coefficient's power (8^(2/3) = 4, times 2), x^(−5/2)/2 gets x⁻⁴ by losing the sign when multiplying −6 by −2/3, x^(11/2)/4 forgets to take the square root of the 4, and 2x^(11/2) leaves the factor 8^(−2/3) out entirely.

Simplify each radical: √50 = 5√2, √18 = 3√2 and √(8/9) = √8/√9 = 2√2/3. Then 5√2 − 3√2 + 2√2/3 = 2√2 + 2√2/3 = 8√2/3. 20√2/9 leaves the 9 under the root (2√2/9), 26√2/3 adds √18 instead of subtracting it, 14√2/3 combines √50 − √18 as √32, and 4√2/3 subtracts the last term instead of adding it.

Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate √5 + √2. Numerator: (√5 + √2)² = 5 + 2√10 + 2 = 7 + 2√10. Denominator: (√5)² − (√2)² = 5 − 2 = 3. So the value is (7 + 2√10)/3. Dividing by 7 adds the squares in the denominator, 3 + 2√10 subtracts them in the numerator, 7 + 2√10 forgets the denominator of 3, and (7 + √10)/3 drops the factor 2 from the middle term of the square.

questions.stem: A thermocouple wire has a diameter of 0.25 mm. What is its cross-sectional area in square meters?
questions.explain: The radius is 0.125 mm = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m, so A = πr² = π(1.25 × 10⁻⁴)² = π × 1.5625 × 10⁻⁸ ≈ 4.91 × 10⁻⁸ m². 1.96 × 10⁻⁷ m² uses the diameter as the radius, 4.91 × 10⁻⁵ m² converts 0.0491 mm² with the linear factor 10⁻³ instead of 10⁻⁶, 3.93 × 10⁻⁴ m² forgets to square the radius, and 4.91 × 10⁻¹⁴ m² converts with 10⁻¹² as if a millimeter were 10⁻⁶ m.

Write both sides as powers of 2: (1/4)^(x − 2) = 2^(−2(x − 2)) = 2^(−2x + 4) and 32^(x + 1) = 2^(5x + 5). Set the exponents equal: −2x + 4 = 5x + 5, so −7x = 1 and x = −1/7. 1/7 is a sign slip in the last step, −9/7 distributes −2(x − 2) as −2x − 4, −3 writes 1/4 as 2² instead of 2⁻², and 3/7 multiplies only the x by 5 (5x + 1).

(2.0 × 10⁻³)⁻² = 2.0⁻² × 10⁶ = 0.25 × 10⁶ = 2.5 × 10⁵. (4.0 × 10²)^(1/2) = 2.0 × 10¹ = 20. Product: 2.5 × 10⁵ × 20 = 5.0 × 10⁶. 8.0 × 10⁻⁵ ignores the negative power and squares 2.0 × 10⁻³ instead, 5.0 × 10⁷ takes the square root of the 4.0 but not of the 10², 5.0 × 10⁵ adds the exponents −3 and −2 instead of multiplying them, and 1.0 × 10⁷ treats 2.0⁻² as 1/2.

questions.stem: Solve the system 3x − 4y = 18 and 5x + 6y = −8. The solution (x, y) is
questions.explain: Eliminate y: multiply the first equation by 3 (9x − 12y = 54) and the second by 2 (10x + 12y = −16), then add: 19x = 38, so x = 2. Then 3(2) − 4y = 18 gives −4y = 12 and y = −3. Check: 5(2) + 6(−3) = −8 ✓. (2, 3) drops the sign of y, (−3, 2) swaps the coordinates, (−2, −6) gets 19x = −38 by subtracting the equations wrongly (it fits the first equation only), and (3, −2) both swaps and changes signs.

questions.stem: Solve |3x + 4| ≥ 11.
questions.explain: A 'greater than or equal' absolute value splits into two separate pieces. 3x + 4 ≥ 11 gives x ≥ 7/3, and 3x + 4 ≤ −11 gives 3x ≤ −15, so x ≤ −5. The answer is x ≤ −5 or x ≥ 7/3. −5 ≤ x ≤ 7/3 is the solution of |3x + 4| ≤ 11, x ≤ −7/3 or x ≥ 5 treats the +4 as −4, x ≥ 7/3 drops the negative case, and x ≤ −7/3 or x ≥ 7/3 adds 4 instead of subtracting it in the negative case.

questions.stem: The displacement of a uniformly accelerating object is s = ut + ½at². Solved for a, this is
questions.explain: Subtract ut: ½at² = s − ut. Multiply by 2: at² = 2(s − ut). Divide by t²: a = 2(s − ut)/t². (s − ut)/(2t²) divides by 2 instead of multiplying, 2s/t² − u forgets that the ut term also gets divided by t² (it should be 2u/t), (2s − ut)/t² doubles s but not ut, and 2(s − u)/t² drops the t from ut.

Multiply every term by 6: 2(2x − 1) − 3(x + 4) > 6, so 4x − 2 − 3x − 12 > 6, x − 14 > 6 and x > 20. Multiplying by a positive number keeps the direction. x > 15 forgets to multiply the right side by 6, x > −4 writes −3(x + 4) as −3x + 12, x < 20 flips the sign for no reason, and x > 12 multiplies only the x by −3 (−3x − 4).

questions.stem: Working together, two pumps fill a tank in 4.8 hours. Working alone, the larger pump would take 4 hours less than the smaller pump. How long would the smaller pump take alone?
questions.explain: Let the smaller pump take x hours, so the larger takes x − 4. Rates add: 1/x + 1/(x − 4) = 1/4.8. Clearing fractions: 4.8(2x − 4) = x(x − 4), so x² − 13.6x + 19.2 = 0 and x = (13.6 ± 10.4)/2 = 12 or 1.6. x = 1.6 would give the larger pump a negative time, so x = 12 h. 8 h is the larger pump's time, 1.6 h keeps the rejected root, 9.6 h assumes the pumps are equal (2 × 4.8), and 8.8 h just adds 4 hours to the combined time.

questions.stem: How many kilograms of pure copper must be melted into 40 kg of an alloy that is 25% copper to produce an alloy that is 40% copper?
questions.explain: The alloy holds 0.25 × 40 = 10 kg of copper. Adding x kg of pure copper: 10 + x = 0.40(40 + x), so 10 + x = 16 + 0.4x, 0.6x = 6 and x = 10 kg. 6 kg forgets that the added copper also raises the total mass, 15 kg divides 6 by 0.40 instead of 0.60, 8 kg divides by 0.75, and 16 kg is the copper a 40 kg batch at 40% would hold.

Two absolute values are equal when the insides are equal or opposite. 2x − 5 = x + 4 gives x = 9. 2x − 5 = −(x + 4) gives 3x = 1, so x = 1/3. Both check: |13| = |13| and |−13/3| = |13/3|. 'x = 9 only' ignores the opposite case, x = 3 writes −(x + 4) as −x + 4, '1/3 only' drops the equal case, and −9 or −1/3 flips both signs.

Multiply through by x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2): 3(x + 2) + (x² − 4) = 12, so x² + 3x − 10 = 0 and (x + 5)(x − 2) = 0. x = 2 makes the original denominators zero, so it is rejected; x = −5 checks (3/(−7) + 1 = 4/7 = 12/21). Keeping x = 2 skips the check, '2 only' keeps the wrong root, 5 is a factoring sign slip, and 'No solution' throws out the valid root as well.

questions.stem: Solve 3x² + 2x − 7 = 0.
questions.explain: x = [−2 ± √(4 + 84)]/6 = (−2 ± √88)/6 = (−2 ± 2√22)/6 = (−1 ± √22)/3. (1 ± √22)/3 uses +b instead of −b, (−1 ± √22)/6 divides only the root by 2 and leaves 6 below, (−1 ± 2√5)/3 computes the discriminant as 84 − 4 = 80, and (−1 ± 2√22)/3 halves the −2 but not the 2√22.

questions.stem: A rectangular storage yard is fenced with 240 m of fencing and split into 3 equal pens by 2 inside fences parallel to the width. What is the largest total area the yard can enclose?
questions.explain: Width w appears 4 times (2 ends + 2 inside fences) and length L twice: 4w + 2L = 240, so L = 120 − 2w and A = w(120 − 2w) = −2w² + 120w. The vertex is at w = 120/4 = 30 m, giving L = 60 m and A = 1,800 m². 3,600 m² ignores the inside fences (a 60 m square), 1,440 m² counts 3 inside fences, 600 m² is the area of one pen, and 1,600 m² assumes the best shape is a square (6w = 240).

questions.stem: For which values of k does x² + (k − 2)x + 9 = 0 have exactly one real root (a repeated root)?
questions.explain: A repeated root needs b² − 4ac = 0: (k − 2)² − 36 = 0, so k − 2 = ±6 and k = 8 or k = −4. 'k = 8 only' forgets the negative square root, 4 or −8 solves k + 2 = ±6, 6 or −6 ignores the −2 inside the coefficient, and 5 or −1 leaves out the 4 in 4ac ((k − 2)² = 9).

questions.stem: The roots of 2x² − 7x + 4 = 0 are r and s. What is r² + s²?
questions.explain: r + s = 7/2 and rs = 4/2 = 2. r² + s² = (r + s)² − 2rs = 49/4 − 4 = 33/4. 41/4 subtracts rs only once, 17/4 uses rs = 4 (not dividing c by a), 49/4 stops at (r + s)², and 41 uses r + s = 7 and rs = 4 without dividing by a at all.

questions.stem: Solve 2x² + x − 15 > 0.
questions.explain: Factor: (2x − 5)(x + 3) > 0, with roots x = 5/2 and x = −3. The parabola opens upward, so it is positive outside the roots: x < −3 or x > 5/2. −3 < x < 5/2 is where it is negative, x < −5/2 or x > 3 flips the signs of the roots, x > 5 forgets to divide by the 2 in 2x − 5, and x > 5/2 drops the left-hand piece.

questions.stem: Which equation has the roots 2 + √3 and 2 − √3?
questions.explain: Sum of roots = 4 and product = (2 + √3)(2 − √3) = 4 − 3 = 1, so the equation is x² − (sum)x + (product) = x² − 4x + 1 = 0. x² + 4x + 1 uses +sum, x² − 4x + 7 multiplies the conjugates as 4 + 3, x² − 4x − 1 takes the product as −1, and x² − 2x + 1 uses half the sum of the roots.

questions.stem: Solve x − 7√x + 12 = 0.
questions.explain: Let u = √x: u² − 7u + 12 = 0, so (u − 3)(u − 4) = 0 and u = 3 or 4. Then x = u² = 9 or 16; both check (9 − 21 + 12 = 0 and 16 − 28 + 12 = 0). 3 or 4 stops at u, '16 only' and '9 only' each throw out a valid root, and 81 or 256 squares twice.

questions.stem: A flare's height is h = −16t² + 64t + 80, with h in feet and t in seconds. For how many seconds is the flare at or above 128 ft?
questions.explain: Set −16t² + 64t + 80 ≥ 128: −16t² + 64t − 48 ≥ 0, divide by −16 (flipping the sign): t² − 4t + 3 ≤ 0, so (t − 1)(t − 3) ≤ 0 and 1 ≤ t ≤ 3. That is 3 − 1 = 2 s. 3 s and 1 s are just the two crossing times, 5 s is when the flare lands, and 4 s is the time between the two moments it is at its launch height of 80 ft.

questions.stem: If f(x) = x² − 3x and g(x) = 2x + 1, solve f(g(x)) = 0.
questions.explain: f(g(x)) = (2x + 1)² − 3(2x + 1) = (2x + 1)(2x + 1 − 3) = (2x + 1)(2x − 2). Setting it to 0: x = −1/2 or x = 1. 0 or 3 solves f(x) = 0 instead, 1/2 or −1 is a sign slip, (3 ± √7)/2 solves g(f(x)) = 2x² − 6x + 1 = 0 (the wrong order), and 3/2 simplifies 2x + 1 − 3 as 2x − 3.

questions.stem: If f(x) = 2 log₃(x − 1) + 5, what is f⁻¹(9)?
questions.explain: f⁻¹(9) is the x with f(x) = 9: 2 log₃(x − 1) = 4, so log₃(x − 1) = 2 and x − 1 = 3² = 9, giving x = 10. 82 forgets to divide by 2 (x − 1 = 3⁴), 8 subtracts 1 from 9 instead of adding, 7 uses 3 × 2 instead of 3², and 3 ignores the logarithm (2(x − 1) + 5 = 9).

questions.stem: What is the domain of f(x) = ln(x + 1)/√(6 − x − x²)?
questions.explain: The log needs x + 1 > 0, so x > −1. The square root sits in the denominator, so it must be strictly positive: 6 − x − x² > 0, x² + x − 6 < 0, (x + 3)(x − 2) < 0 and −3 < x < 2. Both together: −1 < x < 2. −3 < x < 2 ignores the log, −1 < x ≤ 2 lets the denominator be zero, −3 ≤ x ≤ 2 ignores the log and the zero denominator, and x > −1 ignores the root.

questions.stem: If f(x) = 2x² − 5x + 1, then [f(x + h) − f(x)]/h simplifies to
questions.explain: f(x + h) = 2x² + 4xh + 2h² − 5x − 5h + 1. Subtract f(x): 4xh + 2h² − 5h. Divide by h: 4x + 2h − 5. 4x − 5 drops the 2h term (that is the limit as h goes to 0), 4x + h − 5 squares (x + h) without doubling 2h², 2x + 2h − 5 forgets the factor 2 on 2xh, and 4x + 2h − 4 does not cancel the constant 1.

questions.stem: f(x) = 3x − 4 and g(x) = (x + 2)/5. What is (g ∘ f)⁻¹(6)?
questions.explain: (g ∘ f)⁻¹ = f⁻¹ ∘ g⁻¹. g⁻¹(x) = 5x − 2, so g⁻¹(6) = 28. f⁻¹(x) = (x + 4)/3, so f⁻¹(28) = 32/3. Check: f(32/3) = 28 and g(28) = 30/5 = 6 ✓. 44/3 applies the inverses in the wrong order (g⁻¹(f⁻¹(6))), 5/16 is the reciprocal of g(f(6)), 16/5 is g(f(6)) itself, and 8 uses f⁻¹(x) = (x − 4)/3.

questions.stem: A temperature transmitter's output is linear in temperature: 4.0 mA at −20 °C and 20.0 mA at 130 °C. What temperature does an output of 11.2 mA represent?
questions.explain: The span is 150 °C over 16.0 mA, so each mA is 9.375 °C. 11.2 mA is 7.2 mA above 4.0 mA: 7.2 × 9.375 = 67.5 °C above −20 °C, which is 47.5 °C. 67.5 °C forgets the −20 °C starting point, 62.5 °C measures down from 130 °C, 29.5 °C uses a 110 °C span (130 − 20), and 64.0 °C scales 11.2/20 of the span without subtracting the 4.0 mA offset.

questions.stem: f(x) = x² − 4x. For what value of a is f(a) = f(a + 2)?
questions.explain: f(a + 2) = (a + 2)² − 4(a + 2) = a² − 4. Setting a² − 4a = a² − 4 gives a = 1. (The points x = 1 and x = 3 sit symmetrically about the axis x = 2.) a = 2 is the vertex itself, a = −1 is a sign slip, a = 0 is just a root of f, and 'No value' assumes a quadratic never repeats a value.

questions.stem: f(x) = √(x − 1) and f(g(x)) = √(4x² + 3) for all x. What is g(x)?
questions.explain: f(g(x)) = √(g(x) − 1), so g(x) − 1 = 4x² + 3 and g(x) = 4x² + 4. 4x² + 2 subtracts 1 instead of adding it, 4x² + 3 copies the inside without undoing f, 16x⁴ + 4 squares the 4x² again, and 2x + 2 takes the square root of each term.

questions.stem: Solve 2 log₃ x − log₃(x − 2) = 2.
questions.explain: 2 log₃ x = log₃ x², so log₃[x²/(x − 2)] = 2 and x²/(x − 2) = 9. Then x² − 9x + 18 = 0 and (x − 3)(x − 6) = 0. Both roots are greater than 2, so both are valid (check x = 3: 2 − 0 = 2 ✓). '6 only' and '3 only' each throw out a valid root, −3 or −6 is a factoring sign slip, and 18/7 treats 2 log₃ x as log₃ 2x.

questions.stem: Solve 3^(x + 2) = 7^(x − 1), to the nearest hundredth.
questions.explain: Take logs: (x + 2) ln 3 = (x − 1) ln 7, so x ln 3 + 2 ln 3 = x ln 7 − ln 7 and x(ln 7 − ln 3) = 2 ln 3 + ln 7. x = (2.197 + 1.946)/0.847 ≈ 4.89. −4.89 puts ln 3 − ln 7 in the denominator, 0.30 moves ln 7 across without changing its sign, 1.36 adds the logs in the denominator, and −0.30 makes both of those sign errors at once.

questions.stem: Isotope A has a half-life of 6 h and isotope B a half-life of 9 h. A sample starts with 8 times as much activity from A as from B. After how many hours are the two activities equal?
questions.explain: Set 8 · 2^(−t/6) = 2^(−t/9). Since 8 = 2³: 3 − t/6 = −t/9, so 3 = t/6 − t/9 = t/18 and t = 54 h. 9 h assumes they meet after one half-life of B, 10.8 h adds the rates (t/6 + t/9 = 3), 144 h uses 8 instead of log₂ 8 = 3, and 18 h stops at the 1/18 without multiplying by 3.

questions.stem: A bacterial culture grows exponentially from 2,000 cells to 18,000 cells in 6 hours. To the nearest hundred, how many cells are there 10 hours after the start?
questions.explain: The culture multiplies by 9 every 6 hours, so N(t) = 2,000 · 9^(t/6). At t = 10: 9^(10/6) = 3^(10/3) ≈ 38.94, and 2,000 × 38.94 ≈ 77,900. 28,700 assumes linear growth (2,666.7 cells per hour), 30,000 scales the growth factor linearly (9 × 10/6 = 15), 162,000 squares the factor (9² for 10 h), and 7,500 inverts the exponent (9^(6/10)).

questions.stem: An account starts at $5,000 and earns 4.5% interest per year, compounded monthly. To the nearest tenth of a year, how long does it take to reach $8,000?
questions.explain: Solve 8,000 = 5,000(1 + 0.045/12)^(12t): 1.6 = 1.00375^(12t), so 12t = ln 1.6/ln 1.00375 ≈ 125.6 months and t ≈ 10.5 years. 13.3 years uses simple interest (3,000 ÷ 225), 10.7 years compounds yearly, 8.7 years takes 4.5% as 0.45% a month (0.0045) instead of 0.045 ÷ 12 = 0.00375, and 1.1 years uses 0.45 instead of 0.045 for 4.5%.

questions.stem: A sample's count rate is 1,200 cpm at 0900 and 300 cpm at 1500 the same day. What was its count rate at 0700?
questions.explain: The rate falls by 4 = 2² in 6 hours, so the half-life is 3 h. Going back 2 hours from 0900 multiplies by 2^(2/3) ≈ 1.587: 1,200 × 1.587 ≈ 1,905 cpm. 1,500 cpm assumes a straight-line drop of 150 cpm per hour, 2,400 cpm goes back a full half-life, 1,800 cpm multiplies by 1.5, and 1,512 cpm goes back only 1 hour.

4^x = (2^x)², so with u = 2^x: u² − 10u + 16 = 0, (u − 2)(u − 8) = 0, u = 2 or 8. Then 2^x = 2 gives x = 1 and 2^x = 8 gives x = 3. 2 or 8 stops at u, '3 only' and '1 only' each discard a valid root, and log 2 or log 8 takes common logs instead of base-2 logs.

questions.stem: Given log 5 = 0.699, what is log 0.0125?
questions.explain: 0.0125 = 125 × 10⁻⁴ = 5³ × 10⁻⁴, so log 0.0125 = 3(0.699) − 4 = 2.097 − 4 = −1.903. −0.903 uses 10⁻³ (125 × 10⁻³ = 0.125), −2.097 makes the whole log of 125 negative, 2.097 leaves out the power of ten, and −2.903 miscounts the decimal places as 10⁻⁵.

questions.stem: A plant's output is raised 20%, then cut 15%. By what percent must it now be raised so that it ends 10% above the original output?
questions.explain: After the two changes the output is 1.20 × 0.85 = 1.02 times the original. The target is 1.10, so the needed factor is 1.10 ÷ 1.02 ≈ 1.078, a 7.8% raise. 5.0% adds and subtracts the percents (20 − 15 = 5, then 10 − 5), 8.0% is the gap in percentage points of the original, 7.3% divides that gap by 1.10 instead of 1.02, and 10.0% assumes the first two changes cancel.

questions.stem: An item is discounted 12%, and then 8% sales tax is added to the discounted price. The final cost is $237.60. What was the original price?
questions.explain: Final = original × 0.88 × 1.08 = original × 0.9504, so original = 237.60 ÷ 0.9504 = $250.00. $247.50 nets the changes to a 4% discount (237.60 ÷ 0.96), $244.82 reverses by multiplying by 1.12 and 0.92, $247.10 adds 4% back to the final price, and $196.43 treats the discount as a 12% increase.

questions.stem: The force between two point charges is F = kq₁q₂/r². If q₁ increases 50%, q₂ decreases 40% and the separation r increases 20%, the force
questions.explain: New/old = (1.5)(0.6)/(1.2)² = 0.90/1.44 = 0.625, so the force falls 37.5%. 'Falls 10%' ignores the change in r, 'falls 25%' divides by 1.2 without squaring, 'rises 29.6%' multiplies by 1.44 instead of dividing, and 'falls 30%' adds the percent changes (+50 − 40 − 2 × 20).

questions.stem: The safe load on a beam varies directly as its width and the square of its depth, and inversely as its length. A beam 4 in wide, 8 in deep and 12 ft long safely holds 2,400 lb. What does a beam 3 in wide, 10 in deep and 15 ft long safely hold?
questions.explain: Scale each factor: width × 3/4, depth² × (10/8)² = 100/64, length ÷ (15/12), so the load is 2,400 × 0.75 × 1.5625 × 0.8 = 2,250 lb. 1,800 lb does not square the depth ratio, 3,516 lb multiplies by the length ratio instead of dividing, 2,813 lb leaves out the length, and 4,000 lb inverts the width ratio.

questions.stem: A launch travels 36 nautical miles upstream and 36 nautical miles back in a total of 5 hours. The current is 3 knots. What is the launch's speed in still water?
questions.explain: 36/(v − 3) + 36/(v + 3) = 5. Multiply by v² − 9: 72v = 5v² − 45, so 5v² − 72v − 45 = 0 and v = (72 ± √(5,184 + 900))/10 = (72 ± 78)/10 = 15 (the other root is negative). 14.4 knots is the average speed for the trip (72 ÷ 5), 17.4 and 11.4 knots add or subtract the current from that, and 18 knots is the downstream speed.

questions.stem: A ship steams 120 nautical miles at 15 knots and returns over the same route at 24 knots. What is its average speed for the round trip?
questions.explain: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 240 ÷ (120/15 + 120/24) = 240 ÷ (8 + 5) = 240/13 ≈ 18.5 knots. 19.5 knots averages the two speeds, 9.2 knots uses one leg's distance over the total time (the same as forgetting the 2 in 2ab/(a + b)), 13.0 knots is the total time in hours, and 39.0 knots adds the speeds.

questions.stem: A 16 L cooling system holds a 30% glycol mixture. How much of the mixture must be drained and replaced with pure glycol to make the system 50% glycol?
questions.explain: Draining x liters leaves 0.30(16 − x) of glycol; adding x liters of pure glycol gives 0.30(16 − x) + x = 0.50 × 16 = 8. So 4.8 + 0.70x = 8 and x = 3.2/0.70 ≈ 4.57 L. 3.20 L adds glycol without draining any, 6.40 L divides the 3.2 L shortfall by 0.50, 10.67 L divides it by 0.30, and 11.43 L is the amount left in the system, not the amount drained.

questions.stem: A crew of 6 can scrape a hull in 15 days. After the 6 have worked 5 days, 4 more workers join them. Working at the same rate, how many more days does the job take?
questions.explain: The job is 6 × 15 = 90 worker-days. After 5 days, 6 × 5 = 30 are done and 60 remain. With 10 workers that takes 60 ÷ 10 = 6 more days. 9 days scales the whole 15 days by 6/10, 10 days ignores the extra workers, 11 days is the total time from the start, and 15 days divides the remaining 60 worker-days by the 4 new workers only.

questions.stem: Four independent detectors each catch a given fault with probability 0.8. What is the probability that at least three of them catch it?
questions.explain: P(exactly 3) = C(4,3)(0.8)³(0.2) = 4 × 0.512 × 0.2 = 0.4096 and P(all 4) = 0.8⁴ = 0.4096. At least three: 0.4096 + 0.4096 = 0.8192. 0.4096 counts only one of the two cases, 0.5120 leaves out the C(4,3) = 4 orderings (0.1024 + 0.4096), 0.9728 is the probability of at least two, and 0.1808 is the complement (two or fewer).

questions.stem: In how many ways can 6 sailors stand in a line for a photo if two particular sailors must not stand next to each other?
questions.explain: All arrangements: 6! = 720. Arrangements with the two together: treat them as one block, 5! = 120, times 2 orders inside the block = 240. Not together: 720 − 240 = 480. 240 is the 'together' count, 600 forgets the 2 orders inside the block (720 − 120), 720 ignores the restriction, and 360 simply halves the total.

questions.stem: A box holds 10 relays, 4 of which are faulty. Three relays are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that exactly one of them is faulty?
questions.explain: Favorable choices: C(4,1) × C(6,2) = 4 × 15 = 60. Total choices: C(10,3) = 120. Probability = 60/120 = 0.500. 0.432 draws with replacement (3 × 0.4 × 0.6²), 0.400 is just 4/10, 0.167 multiplies (4/10)(6/9)(5/8) for one order only, and 0.833 is the complement of that one-order value.

questions.stem: 2% of parts are defective. An inspection flags 95% of defective parts and also falsely flags 4% of good parts. If a part is flagged, what is the probability that it is defective?
questions.explain: P(flagged and defective) = 0.02 × 0.95 = 0.019. P(flagged and good) = 0.98 × 0.04 = 0.0392. P(defective | flagged) = 0.019/(0.019 + 0.0392) = 0.019/0.0582 ≈ 0.33. 0.95 confuses P(flag | defective) with P(defective | flag), 0.02 ignores the test result, 0.67 is the chance a flagged part is good, and 0.48 divides the true flags by the 4% false-flag rate alone (0.019 ÷ 0.04).

questions.stem: The mean of five readings is 18. Two more readings, x and 2x, are added, and the mean of all seven readings becomes 21. What is x?
questions.explain: The five readings total 5 × 18 = 90. The seven total 7 × 21 = 147, so x + 2x = 147 − 90 = 57 and x = 19. 5 uses 5 × 21 = 105 for the new total, 28.5 sets 2x = 57, 38 is the larger new reading (2x), and 1 divides the change in mean (3) by 3.

questions.stem: What is the population standard deviation of the data set 4, 8, 10, 12, 16?
questions.explain: The mean is 50/5 = 10. Squared deviations: 36, 4, 0, 4, 36, which sum to 80. Population variance = 80/5 = 16, so σ = √16 = 4.00. 16.00 is the variance, 4.47 is the sample standard deviation (√(80/4)), 3.20 is the mean absolute deviation (16/5), and 8.94 is √80 without dividing by n.

questions.stem: If log_b 2 = 0.356 and log_b 3 = 0.565, what is log_b (16/27)?
questions.explain: 16/27 = 2⁴/3³, so log_b (16/27) = 4 log_b 2 − 3 log_b 3 = 1.424 − 1.695 = −0.271. 0.271 subtracts in the wrong order, 0.840 divides the two logs (1.424 ÷ 1.695) instead of subtracting, 3.119 adds them, and −0.209 ignores the powers (log_b 2 − log_b 3).

questions.stem: In an arithmetic sequence the 4th term is 17 and the 11th term is 52. What is the sum of the first 20 terms?
questions.explain: From the 4th to the 11th term is 7 steps: 7d = 52 − 17 = 35, so d = 5 and a₁ = 17 − 3(5) = 2. Then a₂₀ = 2 + 19(5) = 97 and S₂₀ = 20(2 + 97)/2 = 990. 1,040 uses a₂₀ = 2 + 20(5) = 102, 1,980 forgets to halve, 890 backs up 4 steps from the 4th term (a₁ = −3), and 97 is the 20th term, not the sum.

questions.stem: A 20 ft ladder leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of 68° with the level ground. To the nearest tenth of a foot, how high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach?
questions.explain: The ladder is the hypotenuse and the height is the side opposite the 68° angle, so height = 20 sin 68° = 20 × 0.9272 = 18.5 ft. 7.5 ft uses cosine, which gives the distance from the wall. 21.6 ft divides by sin 68° instead of multiplying, 8.1 ft divides by tan 68°, and 49.5 ft multiplies by tan 68°, treating the ladder as a leg.

questions.stem: From the top of a lighthouse 150 ft above sea level, the angle of depression to a boat is 12°. To the nearest foot, how far is the boat from the base of the lighthouse?
questions.explain: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the boat, so tan 12° = 150 ÷ d and d = 150 ÷ tan 12° = 150 ÷ 0.2126 = 706 ft. 32 ft multiplies by tan 12° instead of dividing, 721 ft divides by sin 12° and gives the line of sight from the top, 153 ft divides by cos 12°, and 31 ft multiplies by sin 12°.

questions.stem: A conveyor rises 9 ft over a horizontal run of 24 ft. To the nearest tenth of a degree, what angle does the conveyor make with the horizontal?
questions.explain: Rise and run are the opposite and adjacent sides, so θ = tan⁻¹(9/24) = tan⁻¹(0.375) = 20.6°. 22.0° uses sin⁻¹(0.375), treating the run as the belt length, 68.0° uses cos⁻¹(0.375), and 69.4° is tan⁻¹(24/9), the angle with the vertical. 0.4° reads the calculator's radian answer, 0.36, as degrees.

questions.stem: The hypotenuse of a 30°-60°-90° triangle is 18. What is the length of the longer leg?
questions.explain: The sides of a 30°-60°-90° triangle are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2. The hypotenuse 18 is 2 parts, so one part is 9: the short leg is 9 and the long leg is 9√3. 9 is the short leg, 18√3 multiplies the hypotenuse by √3, 6√3 divides 18 by √3, and 9√2 uses the 45°-45°-90° ratio.

questions.stem: What is the exact value of 2 sin 30° cos 30° + tan 60° ÷ tan 30°?
questions.explain: 2 sin 30° cos 30° = 2 × 1/2 × √3/2 = √3/2, and tan 60° ÷ tan 30° = √3 ÷ (1/√3) = 3, so the total is 3 + √3/2. 3 + √3/4 drops the factor 2, 2 + √3/2 divides the angles (60 ÷ 30 = 2) instead of the tangents, 7/2 uses cos 30° = 1/2, and 1 + √3/2 cancels the two tangents as if they were equal.

questions.stem: From a point on level ground, the angle of elevation to the top of a tower is 35°. After walking 50 m straight toward the tower, the angle of elevation is 52°. To the nearest meter, how tall is the tower?
questions.explain: Let h be the height. The distances from the tower are h ÷ tan 35° and h ÷ tan 52°, and they differ by 50: h(1/tan 35° − 1/tan 52°) = 50, so h = 50 ÷ (1.4281 − 0.7813) = 50 ÷ 0.6469 = 77 m. 86 m divides 50 by tan 52° − tan 35°, 64 m and 35 m treat 50 m as the whole distance at 52° and at 35°, and 15 m uses tan(52° − 35°).

questions.stem: θ is an acute angle with cos θ = 5/13. What is tan θ + sin θ?
questions.explain: With adjacent 5 and hypotenuse 13, the opposite side is √(169 − 25) = 12, so tan θ = 12/5 and sin θ = 12/13. Then 12/5 + 12/13 = 156/65 + 60/65 = 216/65. 209/156 uses tan θ = 5/12 (inverted), 181/65 uses sin θ = 5/13 (the cosine), 17/13 adds sin θ and cos θ, and 4/3 adds numerators and denominators straight across.

questions.stem: An aircraft climbs in a straight line. After flying 12,000 ft along its flight path it has gained 1,500 ft of altitude. To the nearest tenth of a degree, what is the climb angle?
questions.explain: The 12,000 ft flown is the hypotenuse and the 1,500 ft gained is the opposite side, so θ = sin⁻¹(1,500/12,000) = sin⁻¹(0.125) = 7.2°. 7.1° uses tan⁻¹, treating 12,000 ft as ground distance, 82.8° uses cos⁻¹(0.125), 82.9° is tan⁻¹(8) with the ratio upside down, and 0.1° reads the radian result 0.125 as degrees.

questions.stem: To the nearest tenth of a degree, what is an angle of 2.5 radians in degrees?
questions.explain: Multiply radians by 180/π: 2.5 × 180 ÷ π = 450 ÷ 3.1416 = 143.2°. 450.0° multiplies by 180 and forgets to divide by π, 71.6° uses 90/π, 150.0° rounds one radian to 60°, and 0.04° multiplies by π/180, the conversion the wrong way.

questions.stem: A circle has a radius of 15 cm. What is the exact length of the arc cut off by a central angle of 72°?
questions.explain: Convert to radians: 72° = 72π/180 = 2π/5. Then s = rθ = 15 × 2π/5 = 6π cm. 12π cm uses the diameter, 45π cm is the sector area ½r²θ, 3π cm uses πr in place of 2πr for the full circle, and 1,080 cm multiplies 15 by 72 without converting degrees to radians.

questions.stem: A sector of a circle of radius 8 in has a central angle of 3π/8 radians. What is the area of the sector?
questions.explain: Sector area is ½r²θ = ½ × 64 × 3π/8 = 12π in². 3π is the arc length rθ, 24π forgets the ½, 48π uses the diameter 16 as the radius, and 3π/2 multiplies ½ × r × θ without squaring r.

questions.stem: A wheel 26 inches in diameter turns at 300 revolutions per minute. To the nearest whole number, what is the linear speed of a point on the rim in feet per minute?
questions.explain: Each revolution moves a rim point one circumference, 2π × 13 = 26π in. So v = 300 × 26π = 7,800π in/min = 24,504 in/min, and ÷ 12 gives 2,042 ft/min. 4,084 uses 26 in as the radius, 1,021 uses π instead of 2π per turn, 325 forgets the 2π altogether, and 24,504 is the answer in inches per minute.

questions.stem: A turbine shaft turns at 3,600 rpm. What is its angular speed in radians per second?
questions.explain: 3,600 rev/min ÷ 60 = 60 rev/s, and each revolution is 2π rad, so ω = 60 × 2π = 120π rad/s (about 377 rad/s). 60π forgets the 2 in 2π, 7,200π forgets to divide by 60, 60 rad/s reads revolutions per second as radians per second, and 120 drops the π.

questions.stem: Two towns lie on the same line of longitude, one at 40° N and one at 25° N. Taking the Earth's radius as 3,960 miles, what is the distance between them along the Earth's surface, to the nearest mile?
questions.explain: The central angle is 40° − 25° = 15° = π/12 rad, so s = 3,960 × π/12 = 330π = 1,037 miles. 1,034 miles is the straight-line chord 2 × 3,960 × sin 7.5°, which cuts through the Earth. 2,073 uses the diameter, 4,493 adds the latitudes to get 65°, and 59,400 multiplies by 15 without converting to radians.

questions.stem: A pendulum 1.2 m long swings so that its bob travels along an arc of 0.45 m. To the nearest tenth of a degree, through what angle does the pendulum swing?
questions.explain: θ = s ÷ r = 0.45 ÷ 1.2 = 0.375 rad, and 0.375 × 180/π = 21.5°. 0.4° leaves the radian value as degrees, 30.9° converts 0.45 × 1.2 = 0.54 rad, 152.8° converts 1.2 ÷ 0.45 = 2.67 rad (ratio upside down), and 135.0° treats 0.375 as a fraction of a full 360° turn.

questions.stem: The minute hand of a clock is 9 cm long. What exact distance does its tip travel from 12:00 to 12:40?
questions.explain: In 40 minutes the hand turns 40/60 of a circle, 240° = 4π/3 rad, so s = 9 × 4π/3 = 12π cm. 6π cm uses 120°, the angle from the 8 back to the 12, 54π cm is the sector area ½r²θ, 18π cm is the whole circumference, and 24π cm uses the diameter 18 cm as the radius.

questions.stem: What is the exact value of sin(5π/6) − cos(4π/3) + tan(7π/4)?
questions.explain: sin(5π/6) = sin 150° = 1/2, cos(4π/3) = cos 240° = −1/2 and tan(7π/4) = tan 315° = −1. So 1/2 − (−1/2) + (−1) = 0. −1 takes cos 240° as +1/2, 2 takes tan 315° as +1, 1 uses the quadrant I values for every term, and (√3 − 1)/2 uses −√3/2 for cos 240°, which is the sine value.

questions.stem: sin θ = −3/5 and θ lies in quadrant III. What is tan θ + cos θ?
questions.explain: In quadrant III sine and cosine are negative and tangent is positive. cos θ = −4/5 and tan θ = (−3/5) ÷ (−4/5) = 3/4, so 3/4 − 4/5 = 15/20 − 16/20 = −1/20. −31/20 makes tan negative, 31/20 makes cos positive, 8/15 uses tan θ = 4/3 (inverted), and 1/20 flips the sign of both terms.

questions.stem: Find all solutions of 2 cos θ + √3 = 0 for 0 ≤ θ < 2π.
questions.explain: cos θ = −√3/2, so the reference angle is π/6 and cosine is negative in quadrants II and III: θ = π − π/6 = 5π/6 and θ = π + π/6 = 7π/6. π/6 and 11π/6 solve cos θ = +√3/2, 2π/3 and 4π/3 solve cos θ = −1/2, and 5π/6 with 11π/6 or 7π/6 with 11π/6 mix in a quadrant where cosine is positive.

questions.stem: What is the reference angle of −1,000°?
questions.explain: Add 360° until the angle is between 0° and 360°: −1,000° + 3 × 360° = 80°, which lies in quadrant I, so the reference angle is 80°. 280° is coterminal with +1,000°, not −1,000°. 100° and 260° are 180° − 80° and 180° + 80°, and 10° is 90° − 80°. A reference angle is always measured to the x-axis and is never more than 90°.

questions.stem: Which of the following is negative?
questions.explain: 250° is in quadrant III, where sine is negative, so its reciprocal csc 250° is negative too. sin 100° is in quadrant II (sine positive), cos 300° is in quadrant IV (cosine positive), tan 200° is in quadrant III where sine and cosine are both negative so tangent is positive, and sec 80° is in quadrant I.

questions.stem: The terminal side of angle θ in standard position passes through the point (−5, 12). What is sec θ + cot θ?
questions.explain: r = √(25 + 144) = 13, so sec θ = r/x = 13/(−5) and cot θ = x/y = −5/12. The sum is −156/60 − 25/60 = −181/60. 131/60 makes sec positive, −131/60 makes cot positive, −5 uses tan θ = −12/5 in place of cot θ, and 2/3 uses csc θ = 13/12 in place of sec θ.

questions.stem: tan θ = −2 and cos θ > 0. What is the exact value of sin θ?
questions.explain: tan negative with cos positive puts θ in quadrant IV, where sine is negative. With opposite 2 and adjacent 1, the hypotenuse is √5, so sin θ = −2/√5 = −2√5/5. 2√5/5 has the wrong sign, −√5/5 is the cosine's size with sine's sign, −2/3 adds the legs to get the hypotenuse, and −2√3/3 uses √3 as the hypotenuse.

questions.stem: What is the exact value of cos(−π/3) + sin(−7π/6)?
questions.explain: Cosine is even, so cos(−π/3) = cos(π/3) = 1/2. Sine is odd, so sin(−7π/6) = −sin(7π/6) = −(−1/2) = 1/2. The total is 1. 0 forgets to flip the sign for the negative angle, −1 treats cosine as odd too, and (1 + √3)/2 and (1 − √3)/2 use √3/2 for sin(7π/6), mixing it up with the cosine.

questions.stem: What are the period and the phase shift of y = −3 sin(4x − π) + 2?
questions.explain: Write it as −3 sin(4(x − π/4)) + 2. The period is 2π/4 = π/2 and the shift is π/4 to the right. Shift π right forgets to factor out the 4, period 8π multiplies 2π by 4, shift left misreads the sign of x − π/4, and period 4 reads the coefficient itself as the period.

questions.stem: What is the range of y = 5 − 2 cos(3x)?
questions.explain: cos(3x) runs from −1 to 1, so −2 cos(3x) runs from −2 to 2, and adding 5 gives 3 to 7. −2 to 2 forgets the vertical shift, 2 to 8 takes the 3 inside the cosine as the amplitude, 5 to 7 keeps only the top half of the swing, and −7 to −3 changes the sign of the whole function because of the minus.

questions.stem: The height of a seat on a Ferris wheel is h(t) = 22 − 20 cos(πt/6) meters, where t is in minutes. What is the height of the seat at t = 4 minutes?
questions.explain: At t = 4, πt/6 = 2π/3 and cos(2π/3) = −1/2, so h = 22 − 20(−1/2) = 22 + 10 = 32 m. 12 m uses cos(2π/3) = +1/2, 42 m is the maximum height, 2 m evaluates cos 2.09 in degree mode, which is almost 1, and 4.7 m uses sine in place of cosine.

questions.stem: What is the period of y = tan(πx/4)?
questions.explain: Tangent repeats every π, so the period of tan(bx) is π/b = π ÷ (π/4) = 4. 8 uses 2π, the period of sine and cosine. 1/4 inverts the division, 4π divides π by 1/4 and ignores the π inside, and π/4 reads the coefficient as the period.

questions.stem: A tide reaches a high of 9.4 ft at 3:00 a.m. and the next low of 1.2 ft at 9:15 a.m. Modeled as a sinusoid, what are the amplitude and the period?
questions.explain: Amplitude is half the distance from high to low: (9.4 − 1.2) ÷ 2 = 4.1 ft. High to the next low is half a cycle, 6 h 15 min = 6.25 h, so the period is 12.5 h. 8.2 ft forgets to halve, 6.25 h is only half a cycle, 5.3 ft is the midline height, and 12.3 h reads 6 h 15 min as 6.15 h.

questions.stem: How many solutions does 2 sin(3x) = 1 have for 0 ≤ x < 2π?
questions.explain: sin(3x) = 1/2. As x runs from 0 to 2π, 3x runs from 0 to 6π, three full cycles, and sine equals 1/2 twice in every cycle, so there are 6 solutions. 2 counts only one cycle, 3 counts one solution per cycle, 12 doubles the cycles a second time, and 4 counts two cycles.

questions.stem: A cosine curve has amplitude 4, period 6π, a maximum at x = 0 and a midline of y = −1. Which equation describes it?
questions.explain: A cosine with a maximum at x = 0 needs no shift. The period 2π/b = 6π gives b = 1/3, so y = 4 cos(x/3) − 1. cos(3x) has period 2π/3, y = −cos(x/3) + 4 swaps the amplitude and the midline, the sine version starts on the midline instead of at a maximum, and cos(x/6) has period 12π.

questions.stem: For x ≥ 0, where does y = 2 cos(x + π/3) reach its first maximum?
questions.explain: Cosine is at its maximum when its input is 0, 2π, 4π and so on. x + π/3 = 0 gives x = −π/3, which is before 0, so the first maximum is at x + π/3 = 2π, x = 5π/3. π/3 shifts the wrong way, 2π/3 is where the input is π, a minimum, 7π/3 adds π/3 to 2π, and π/6 is where the curve crosses its midline.

questions.stem: For values where it is defined, (1 − cos²θ) ÷ (sin θ cos θ) simplifies to
questions.explain: 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ, so the expression is sin²θ ÷ (sin θ cos θ) = sin θ ÷ cos θ = tan θ. cot θ cancels the wrong way, sin θ forgets to divide by cos θ, sec θ cancels the sin θ factors completely, and 1 treats 1 − cos²θ as sin θ cos θ.

questions.stem: sin θ = 0.6 and π/2 < θ < π. What is sin 2θ?
questions.explain: In quadrant II cosine is negative: cos θ = −√(1 − 0.36) = −0.8. Then sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ = 2(0.6)(−0.8) = −0.96. 0.96 takes cos θ as positive, 1.2 doubles sin θ, 0.28 is cos 2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ, and 0.36 squares sin θ.

questions.stem: θ is an acute angle with tan θ = 3/4. What is cos 2θ?
questions.explain: From a 3-4-5 triangle, cos θ = 4/5 and sin θ = 3/5, so cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 16/25 − 9/25 = 7/25. 24/25 is sin 2θ, −7/25 subtracts in the wrong order, 8/5 is 2 cos θ, and 1/5 subtracts cos θ and sin θ without squaring them.

questions.stem: For values where it is defined, sec θ − tan θ sin θ simplifies to
questions.explain: Write everything in sine and cosine: 1/cos θ − sin²θ/cos θ = (1 − sin²θ)/cos θ = cos²θ/cos θ = cos θ. sin θ uses 1 − cos²θ by mistake, sec θ drops the second term, 1 treats 1 − sin²θ as cos θ, and csc θ swaps sine and cosine throughout.

questions.stem: If sin θ + cos θ = 1.2, what is sin θ cos θ?
questions.explain: Square both sides: sin²θ + 2 sin θ cos θ + cos²θ = 1.44. Since sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 2 sin θ cos θ = 0.44 and sin θ cos θ = 0.22. 0.44 forgets to divide by 2, 0.72 halves 1.44 without subtracting the 1, 0.6 halves 1.2, and 1.44 just squares the sum.

questions.stem: Using cos 75° = cos(45° + 30°), what is the exact value of cos 75°?
questions.explain: cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B = (√2/2)(√3/2) − (√2/2)(1/2) = √6/4 − √2/4 = (√6 − √2)/4. (√6 + √2)/4 adds the terms, which is cos 15°. (√2 + √3)/2 adds cos 45° and cos 30°, √6/4 drops the second term, and (√3 − 1)/4 leaves the √2 out of both products.

questions.stem: Find all solutions of 2cos²x − cos x − 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ x < 360°.
questions.explain: Factor: (2 cos x + 1)(cos x − 1) = 0, so cos x = −1/2 or cos x = 1. cos x = 1 at 0°, and cos x = −1/2 at 120° and 240°. 120°, 240° drops cos x = 1, 0°, 60°, 300° uses cos x = +1/2, 0°, 120° misses the quadrant III answer, and 60°, 180°, 300° comes from factoring with the signs reversed.

questions.stem: For values where it is defined, tan θ + cot θ simplifies to
questions.explain: Over a common denominator, sin θ/cos θ + cos θ/sin θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(sin θ cos θ) = sec θ csc θ. 1 multiplies tan θ and cot θ instead of adding them, sin θ cos θ is the reciprocal of the right answer, 2 assumes tan θ = cot θ, and sec²θ is 1 + tan²θ.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, a = 8, b = 11 and angle C = 47°. To the nearest tenth, what is side c?
questions.explain: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C = 64 + 121 − 176 cos 47° = 185 − 120.0 = 65.0, so c = 8.1. 17.5 adds the 2ab cos C term, 11.2 leaves out the 2, 19.0 comes from a calculator in radian mode (cos 47 rad is about −0.99), and 65.0 is c² with no square root.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, A = 40°, B = 65° and a = 12. To the nearest tenth, what is side b?
questions.explain: By the law of sines, b = a sin B ÷ sin A = 12 × 0.9063 ÷ 0.6428 = 16.9. 8.5 inverts the ratio, 18.0 uses C = 75°, which gives side c, 19.5 scales by the angles themselves (12 × 65/40), and 10.9 multiplies by sin 65° without dividing by sin 40°.

questions.stem: Two sides of a triangle are 14 cm and 9 cm, and the angle between them is 135°. To the nearest tenth, what is the area of the triangle?
questions.explain: Area = ½ab sin C = ½ × 14 × 9 × sin 135° = 63 × 0.7071 = 44.5 cm². 89.1 forgets the ½, 63.0 leaves out the sine, 5.6 comes from radian mode (sin 135 rad is about 0.09), and 22.3 takes half a second time.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, A = 35°, a = 9 and b = 14. How many triangles fit these measurements?
questions.explain: This is the SSA case. The height from C is b sin A = 14 sin 35° = 8.03. Since 8.03 < a = 9 < b = 14, side a can swing to meet the base in two places, so there are two triangles: sin B = 14 sin 35° ÷ 9 = 0.892, giving B = 63.2° or B = 116.8°. Picking only one of these misses the other, None would need a < 8.03, and a right triangle would need a = 8.03 exactly.

questions.stem: Two ships leave port at the same time. One sails 18 nautical miles on a bearing of 050°, and the other sails 25 nautical miles on a bearing of 160°. To the nearest tenth of a nautical mile, how far apart are they?
questions.explain: The angle between the bearings is 160° − 50° = 110°. d² = 18² + 25² − 2(18)(25) cos 110° = 949 + 307.8 = 1,256.8, so d = 35.5 nmi. 25.3 subtracts the cosine term as if cos 110° were positive, 30.8 treats the angle as 90°, 43.0 adds the distances, and 41.6 adds the bearings to get 210°.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 7, 10 and 13. To the nearest tenth of a degree, what is its largest angle?
questions.explain: The largest angle is opposite the longest side: cos C = (49 + 100 − 169) ÷ (2 × 7 × 10) = −20/140 = −1/7, so C = 98.2°. 81.8° drops the minus sign, 106.6° divides by 70 instead of 140, 32.2° is the smallest angle (opposite 7), and 1.7° is the radian answer, 1.71, read as degrees.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, A = 30°, a = 10 and c = 16. If angle C is acute, what is C to the nearest tenth of a degree?
questions.explain: sin C = c sin A ÷ a = 16 × 0.5 ÷ 10 = 0.8, so C = sin⁻¹(0.8) = 53.1°. 126.9° is the obtuse solution, which the question rules out. 18.2° inverts the ratio (10 × 0.5 ÷ 16), 36.9° uses cos⁻¹(0.8), and 48.0° scales the angle by the sides (30 × 16/10).

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, b = 20, A = 50° and C = 70°. To the nearest tenth, what is the area of the triangle?
questions.explain: B = 180° − 50° − 70° = 60°. By the law of sines a = 20 sin 50° ÷ sin 60° = 17.69. The angle between sides a and b is C, so area = ½ab sin C = ½ × 17.69 × 20 × sin 70° = 166.2. 153.2 uses sin B in the area formula, 332.5 forgets the ½, 187.9 takes a = 20, and 212.5 inverts the law of sines ratio for a.

questions.stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures 162°. How many diagonals does the polygon have?
questions.explain: Each exterior angle is 180° − 162° = 18°, and exterior angles total 360°, so n = 360 ÷ 18 = 20 sides. Diagonals = n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 20 × 17 ÷ 2 = 170. 340 forgets to divide by 2, 190 is n(n − 1) ÷ 2, which also counts the 20 sides, 180 uses n(n − 2) ÷ 2, and 17 counts only the diagonals from one vertex.

questions.stem: Two similar triangles have areas of 48 cm² and 108 cm². The smaller triangle has a perimeter of 24 cm. What is the perimeter of the larger triangle?
questions.explain: Areas scale by the square of the length ratio: 108/48 = 2.25 = 1.5², so lengths scale by 1.5 and the perimeter is 24 × 1.5 = 36 cm. 54 cm scales the perimeter by the area ratio 2.25, 16 cm divides by 1.5, 84 cm adds the 60 cm² difference in area, and 10.7 cm multiplies by 48/108.

questions.stem: A chord 16 cm long is 6 cm from the center of a circle. What is the circumference of the circle?
questions.explain: The perpendicular from the center bisects the chord, so half the chord (8), the distance (6) and the radius form a right triangle: r = √(64 + 36) = 10 and C = 2πr = 20π cm. 10π uses πr, 100π is the area, 4√73π uses the whole chord 16 as a leg, and 4√55π subtracts 36 from 256.

questions.stem: Two chords intersect inside a circle. The angle they form intercepts an arc of 124°, and its vertical angle intercepts an arc of 46°. What is the measure of the angle?
questions.explain: An angle formed by two chords crossing inside a circle is half the sum of the intercepted arcs: (124° + 46°) ÷ 2 = 85°. 170° forgets to halve, 39° uses half the difference, which is the rule for angles outside the circle, 62° uses only one arc, and 95° is the supplementary angle beside it.

questions.stem: From a point P outside a circle, a tangent segment PT is 12 long. A secant from P meets the circle first at A and then at B, with PA = 8. What is the length of chord AB?
questions.explain: By the tangent-secant theorem, PT² = PA × PB, so 144 = 8 × PB and PB = 18. The chord is AB = PB − PA = 18 − 8 = 10. 18 is the whole secant, 4 is 12 − 8, 4√5 = √(144 − 64) treats the segments as a right triangle, and 26 adds PA and PB.

questions.stem: What is the exact area of a regular hexagon with sides of 10 cm?
questions.explain: A regular hexagon is six equilateral triangles, each with area (√3/4)s² = (√3/4)(100) = 25√3, so the total is 150√3 cm² (about 259.8). 300√3 uses √3/2 in place of √3/4, 25√3 is one triangle only, 300 uses ½ × 10 × 10 as if each triangle were right-angled, and 75√3 uses half the apothem, 5√3 ÷ 2.

questions.stem: A circular garden 20 ft in diameter is surrounded by a path 3 ft wide. What is the exact area of the path?
questions.explain: The garden's radius is 10 ft and the outer radius is 10 + 3 = 13 ft, so the path is π(13² − 10²) = π(169 − 100) = 69π ft². 9π is the area of a circle of radius 3, 60π multiplies the inner circumference by the width, 276π uses diameters in place of radii, and 32.25π adds the 3 ft to the diameter instead of the radius.

questions.stem: The altitude to the hypotenuse of a right triangle divides the hypotenuse into segments of 4 and 9. How long is the altitude?
questions.explain: The altitude to the hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two segments: h² = 4 × 9 = 36, so h = 6. 6.5 is the ordinary average, √97 treats 4 and 9 as legs, 36 forgets the square root, and 2√13 is the shorter leg, √(4 × 13).

questions.stem: A cylindrical tank is 8 ft in diameter and 12 ft tall. One cubic foot holds 7.48 gallons. To the nearest gallon, how much does the full tank hold?
questions.explain: V = πr²h = π × 4² × 12 = 192π = 603.2 ft³, and 603.2 × 7.48 = 4,512 gallons. 18,047 uses the diameter as the radius, 603 forgets to convert to gallons, 81 divides by 7.48, and 2,256 uses the curved surface area 2πrh in place of the volume.

questions.stem: A sphere has a surface area of 144π cm². What is its volume?
questions.explain: 4πr² = 144π gives r² = 36 and r = 6, so V = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3)π(216) = 288π cm³. 216π forgets the 4/3, 864π uses 4πr³, 48π squares the radius instead of cubing it, and 2,304π solves πr² = 144π and gets r = 12, forgetting the 4.

questions.stem: A cone has a base radius of 6 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explain: The height, radius and slant height form a right triangle: h = √(100 − 36) = 8. Then V = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(36)(8) = 96π cm³. 120π uses the slant height as the height, 288π forgets the 1/3, 60π is the curved surface area πrl, and 360π both forgets the 1/3 and uses the slant height.

questions.stem: A model ship is built to a scale of 1:40. The model's surface area is 150 cm². What is the surface area of the real ship?
questions.explain: Areas scale by the square of the length ratio: 150 × 40² = 240,000 cm². There are 100 × 100 = 10,000 cm² in 1 m², so the real area is 24 m². 0.6 m² scales by 40 instead of 40², 960 m² scales by 40³, 240 m² divides by 1,000, and 2,400 m² divides by only 100, treating cm² like cm.

questions.stem: Two similar cones have heights of 4 cm and 10 cm. The smaller cone has a volume of 24 cm³. What is the volume of the larger cone?
questions.explain: The length ratio is 10/4 = 2.5, and volumes scale by its cube: 24 × 2.5³ = 24 × 15.625 = 375 cm³. 60 scales by 2.5 once, 150 scales by 2.5², which is the area ratio, 9.6 divides by 2.5, and 937.5 uses the fourth power.

questions.stem: A rectangular box measures 3 in by 4 in by 12 in, with the 12 in edge vertical. To the nearest tenth of a degree, what angle does the box's space diagonal make with the base?
questions.explain: The diagonal of the 3 × 4 base is 5, and the space diagonal rises 12 above it, so the angle is tan⁻¹(12/5) = 67.4°. 22.6° is tan⁻¹(5/12), the angle with the vertical. 71.6° and 76.0° use only one base edge, 4 or 3, in place of the base diagonal, and 59.7° adds 3 + 4 instead of using Pythagoras.

questions.stem: A pyramid has a square base 10 m on each side and a slant height of 13 m, measured up the middle of each triangular face. What is its volume?
questions.explain: The height, half the base (5) and the slant height form a right triangle: h = √(169 − 25) = 12. V = (1/3) × base area × h = (1/3)(100)(12) = 400 m³. 433.3 uses the slant height as the height, 1,200 forgets the 1/3, 260 is the lateral area 4 × ½ × 10 × 13, and 360 is the total surface area.

questions.stem: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted down and recast as a solid cylinder of radius 4 cm. How tall is the cylinder?
questions.explain: Volume is conserved: (4/3)π(6³) = 288π, and π(4²)h = 16πh, so h = 288 ÷ 16 = 18 cm. 13.5 forgets the 4/3 (216 ÷ 16), 9 matches the sphere's surface area 144π instead of its volume, 72 divides by r instead of r², and 4.5 uses the cylinder's diameter (8² = 64).

questions.stem: What is the distance between the points (−3, 7) and (5, −8)?
questions.explain: The changes are 5 − (−3) = 8 and −8 − 7 = −15, so d = √(8² + 15²) = √289 = 17. 23 adds the changes without Pythagoras, √5 adds the coordinates instead of subtracting them, giving changes of 2 and −1, 15 is the vertical change only, and 8.5 halves the distance as if finding the midpoint.

questions.stem: Which line passes through (4, −1) and is perpendicular to 3x − 2y = 6?
questions.explain: 3x − 2y = 6 rearranges to y = (3/2)x − 3, slope 3/2, so the perpendicular slope is −2/3. Through (4, −1): y + 1 = −(2/3)(x − 4), y = −(2/3)x + 8/3 − 1 = −(2/3)x + 5/3. (3/2)x − 7 is the parallel line, (2/3)x − 11/3 forgets the negative, −(3/2)x + 5 forgets the reciprocal, and −(2/3)x + 11/3 uses y − 1 instead of y + 1.

questions.stem: What are the center and radius of the circle x² + y² − 6x + 10y − 2 = 0?
questions.explain: Complete the squares: (x² − 6x + 9) + (y² + 10y + 25) = 2 + 9 + 25, so (x − 3)² + (y + 5)² = 36. The center is (3, −5) and the radius is 6. (−3, 5) flips both signs, radius 36 forgets the square root, √32 moves the 2 to the wrong side, and (6, −10) forgets to halve the coefficients.

questions.stem: M(2, −3) is the midpoint of segment AB, and A is (−4, 5). What are the coordinates of B?
questions.explain: B = 2M − A = (2 × 2 − (−4), 2 × (−3) − 5) = (8, −11). Check: the midpoint of (−4, 5) and (8, −11) is (2, −3). (−1, 1) is the midpoint of A and M, (6, −8) is M − A, (−10, 13) is 2A − M, extending the wrong way, and (8, −1) adds 5 instead of subtracting it.

questions.stem: The angle of inclination of a line is the angle from 0° up to 180° that it makes with the positive x-axis. To the nearest tenth of a degree, what is the angle of inclination of 2x + 5y = 7?
questions.explain: The slope is −2/5. tan⁻¹(−0.4) = −21.8°, and since the inclination must be between 0° and 180°, add 180° to get 158.2°. 21.8° drops the negative slope, 68.2° and 111.8° use the slope 5/2 upside down, and −21.8° is the raw calculator output, which is outside the allowed range.

questions.stem: What is the area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (8, 2) and (3, 7)?
questions.explain: With one vertex at the origin, area = ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁| = ½|8 × 7 − 3 × 2| = ½|56 − 6| = 25. 50 forgets the ½, 31 adds the cross products instead of subtracting, 28 uses ½ × 8 × 7 as if the triangle were right-angled, and 12.5 halves twice.

questions.stem: Which point lies on the circle (x + 2)² + (y − 1)² = 25?
questions.explain: The center is (−2, 1) and the radius is 5. For (1, 5): (1 + 2)² + (5 − 1)² = 9 + 16 = 25, so it lies on the circle. (5, 3) and (−1, −5) lie on (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25, the circle with the center's signs flipped. (3, 6) moves 5 in both directions, giving 50, and (0, 6) gives 4 + 25 = 29.

questions.stem: What is the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining (−2, 3) and (6, −1)?
questions.explain: The midpoint is ((−2 + 6)/2, (3 − 1)/2) = (2, 1). The segment's slope is (−1 − 3)/(6 + 2) = −1/2, so the perpendicular slope is 2: y − 1 = 2(x − 2), y = 2x − 3. −(1/2)x + 2 uses the segment's own slope, −2x + 5 forgets the reciprocal's sign change, (1/2)x forgets the negative, and 2x − 2 subtracts the y-values when averaging, (3 − (−1)) ÷ 2 = 2, giving a midpoint of (2, 2).

questions.stem: From the top of a cliff 60 m above sea level, the angles of depression to two buoys in a straight line on the same side of the cliff are 41° and 28°. To the nearest meter, how far apart are the buoys?
